weather.tip: Light drizzle with a 100% rain chance through the evening — carry an umbrella, avoid low-lying underpasses on your way home, and budget extra time for the commute.

around.headline: Masked men attack people with machetes 'indiscriminately' in Uttarahalli, four injured
around.summary: A group of masked men wielding machetes attacked people at random in Bengaluru's Uttarahalli, injuring four, per Deccan Herald. If you're in the area this evening, avoid the locality until police confirm the attackers are in custody, and keep an emergency number on speed dial.

around.headline: One killed after tempo traveller overturns avoiding motorcyclists doing wheelies
around.summary: A tempo traveller overturned and killed one person after the driver apparently swerved to avoid motorcyclists performing wheelies on the road, per Deccan Herald. Keep extra distance from bikers riding recklessly rather than braking or swerving hard, which can be just as dangerous.

around.headline: BDA seeks nod to fell 1,128 trees for Hebbal short tunnel; citizens push back
around.summary: The Bengaluru Development Authority wants permission to cut 1,128 trees for the Hebbal short-tunnel project, and GBA has invited public objections, while citizens' groups say the plan threatens nearby lakes, per The Hindu and The Times of India. If you live near Hebbal, this is the window to file an objection before felling is approved.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Report: you'd need a ₹70,000 salary to afford daily Namma Metro travel
around.summary: A fare-affordability analysis says a Bengaluru commuter needs roughly a ₹70,000 monthly salary for Namma Metro to be an affordable daily commute option, sparking criticism of the fare structure, per The Hindu and News18. If metro fares are straining your budget, look at monthly/weekly pass options or BMTC feeder buses for part of the route.

around.headline: Ganesha immersion drive causes traffic disruption tonight; over 4 lakh idols immersed so far
around.summary: More than four lakh Ganesha idols have been immersed across the city in the past week, with processions and lake-side crowds continuing to disrupt traffic this evening, per The Siasat Daily and FM Bharat. Expect diversions near immersion lakes and give processions extra time rather than trying to push through.

around.headline: Tanker hit near Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran tensions escalate; India weighs new US tariffs on Russian oil buyers
around.summary: A projectile hit a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz with two crew injured amid rising US-Iran tensions, even as India examines new US tariff powers targeting buyers of Russian oil, per The Indian Express and The Times of India. Both point to possible upward pressure on fuel prices in the coming weeks — worth watching if you're budgeting for a fuel-heavy commute.
around.source: The Indian Express, The Times of India

street_smart.title: You're walking through a crowded lane in your Bengaluru neighbourhood this evening when you hear screams up ahead — a group of masked men are attacking people with machetes, seemingly at random, and people are running past you in panic. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Deccan Herald, Sept 21 — masked men wielding machetes attacked people 'indiscriminately' in Bengaluru's Uttarahalli, injuring four. This bystander-response-to-an-active-public-weapon-attack mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The attackers are still in the lane, about 50 metres away, and you can't immediately tell who's a target versus a bystander. Your phone is in your pocket, and the nearest shop with a shutter is a few steps behind you.

choices.text: Turn and move quickly in the opposite direction to a safe distance, get behind solid cover, and call the police (100) with your exact location once you're safe.
choices.feedback: Correct. The standard response to an active weapon attack is Run, Hide, then Tell — put distance and cover between yourself and the attackers first, and only call police once you're no longer in reach; a shaky, panicked call made while still in danger helps no one.

choices.text: Move closer to get a clear phone video of the attack to post online and warn others.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Filming from close range keeps you inside the attackers' reach and slows down your own escape. Footage doesn't help anyone being attacked right now — it can be handed to police afterward by people who were already safely clear of the scene.

choices.text: Try to reach the nearest injured person and help them immediately, even though the attackers are still nearby.
choices.feedback: Risky. The instinct is understandable, but stepping toward an active weapon attack can turn you into a second victim and complicate any rescue. Get to safety first, then alert emergency responders, who are trained and equipped to reach the injured safely.

choices.text: Duck into the nearest shop and pull the shutter down, without telling anyone what's happening or calling for help.
choices.feedback: Risky. Taking cover is right, but staying silent delays the police response and leaves other people in the lane unwarned. Combine sheltering with calling 100 as soon as it's safe, and shout a warning to others nearby if you can do so without exposing yourself.

takeaways: In an active weapon attack, follow Run (put distance between you and the threat), Hide (get behind solid cover), then Tell (call police) — in that order; don't stop to film or intervene while attackers are still active nearby.
Karnataka's police emergency number is 100, and 112 is the unified all-in-one emergency helpline — give your exact location and a description of the attackers before hanging up.
Once you're safe, a shouted warning to people still approaching the area can help more bystanders get clear before police arrive.

quiz.question: How many people were injured today when masked men wielding machetes attacked people 'indiscriminately' in Bengaluru's Uttarahalli?
quiz.why: The attack was described as indiscriminate, meaning bystanders were targeted at random rather than a specific individual — the pattern police typically associate with gang turf disputes spilling into public streets.

quiz.question: The Bengaluru Development Authority (BDA) is seeking permission to fell how many trees for the Hebbal short-tunnel project, drawing objections from citizens?
quiz.why: Citizens' groups opposing the felling have specifically linked it to threats to nearby lakes, since tree cover around urban lakes helps recharge groundwater and reduce runoff.

quiz.question: A fare-affordability report published today says a Bengaluru commuter would need roughly what monthly salary for daily Namma Metro travel to be considered affordable?
quiz.why: Affordability benchmarks for public transport commonly cap commute costs at around 5-10% of income — a threshold Namma Metro's current fares are reported to exceed for most salaried commuters.

quiz.question: The Strait of Hormuz, where a tanker was hit today amid rising US-Iran tensions, is the narrow passage connecting the Persian Gulf to which body of water?
quiz.why: Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through this strait, so any disruption there tends to move global crude prices almost immediately.

quiz.question: Karnataka's Kolar Gold Fields, once among the world's deepest mines, was historically worked to extract which precious metal?
quiz.why: At over 3 km deep, KGF was one of the deepest gold mines on the planet before mining operations there shut down in 2001.
